citation: Jensen, Sifnaios and Anderson (2022). twoaxistracking: a Python package for simulating self-shading of two-axis tracking solar collectors. MethodsX 9, 101876. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mex.2022.101876
description: twoaxistracking simulates self-shading among solar collectors that track the sun on two axes. The pvlib-linked research team publishes a Python package, online documentation and a MethodsX paper describing the calculation. A user supplies collector geometry, field layout, solar position and site latitude; the package estimates mutual shading and the effect of spacing and aperture shape over a selected sun-position series. Geography is a user-selected collector field, and temporal resolution follows the provided sun angles or weather series. The source is free under BSD-3-Clause and installable from PyPI. A limitation is that shading estimates are one part of energy yield and do not replace electrical or thermal equipment models. The package supports solar farm layout and output simulations. The catalogue's model-energyplus can account for whole-building energy use but is a different scale of model; no connection was tested. No weather series or example was run.
name: twoaxistracking solar collector shading model
